Sam (support): getting pings from 3 customers — timeouts -> 503s from hosted inference around 06:40 UTC. high error rate on /v1/generate. Can eng-oncall look?
Kevin (eng-oncall): on it. seeing spike in gateway 503s, correlating with worker restarts. any recent deploys?
Sam (support): no customer-side changes. one report includes streaming disconnect + 502->503. CS flagged billing noise for retried calls.
Maria (infra): I see repeated container exits in pool gpu-pool-3, worker ids 176-190. Crash loop started ~06:39. grabbing logs.
ops-bot: alert: hosted-api error-rate 5xx > 3% (5m) — routing fallback triggered for tier=free customers.
Kevin (eng-oncall): log snippet from worker-183: ```
[06:39:58Z] infer-runner[pid=182]: runtime: allocation failed: std::bad_alloc
[06:40:00Z] infer-runner[pid=182]: CUDA error: out of memory while allocating 2147483648 bytes
[06:40:01Z] infer-runner[pid=182]: received SIGSEGV (signal 11)
Stack: 0x7f9a3a12, 0x7f9a3c04, 0x400f12
```
Rana (sdet): repro steps? I can try a synthetic burst of embed+generate with long context.
Olivia (customer-success): customer A reported 503s on 06:40 UTC, impact: ~10% requests failed for 90s. they want ETA.
Kevin (eng-oncall): mitigation: 1) divert traffic from gpu-pool-3 -> gpu-pool-1 for hosted tier=paid; 2) bump retry window for streaming to 8s; 3) pin critical customers to fallback model small-davinci-v1. Doing 1 now.
Maria (infra): reroute done for paid tenants. free tier still on fallback routing by ops-bot.
Sam (support): updated CS with short note. asking for RCA and repro steps.
Rana (sdet): repro attempt: ran `ab -n 100 -c 8` + payload with 64k tokens context hitting model swap. I saw one worker exit with same SIGSEGV after ~40 requests. attaching minimal curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"big-embed-gen","prompt":"<large context>","max_tokens":512}'
```
Response: 503 Service Unavailable after 2s of stall.
Kevin (eng-oncall): interesting — this cluster got a runtime tweak last night: qbatcher v0.9.4 dynamic-resize enabled. Maria, can you check if qbatcher upgrade landed on gpu-pool-3?
Maria (infra): yes, qbatcher v0.9.4 rolled to gpu-pool-3 at 02:12 UTC for a subset of nodes (canary). Looks like the canary expanded during autoscale.
Kevin (eng-oncall): hypothesis: dynamic-resize + large embed bursts -> allocator fragmentation -> OOM -> segfault. Need coredump and cuda logs. Collecting /var/crash and nvml logs now.
ops-bot: note: created incident-1799998888, severity=P2.
Rana (sdet): grabbed a heap profile and core for worker-183: `/tmp/core.worker-183` and `/tmp/heap.worker-183.prof` on node gpunode-12. Uploading to S3: s3://redwood-debug/1799998888/
Kevin (eng-oncall): reversion plan: roll qbatcher back to v0.9.3 on affected nodes and redeploy. Preparing rollout — will drain one node then roll, verify, then expand.
Maria (infra): starting rollback on gpunode-12. will coordinate with autoscaler to prevent new canary expansion.
Olivia (customer-success): any ETA to share? customers asking for timeline.
Kevin (eng-oncall): quick ETA: full rollback of canary subset in ~12 minutes. will watch 5m window for worker restarts.
Sam (support): told customers: engineers investigating, routing mitigations in place, rollback in progress.
Maria (infra): rollback finished on canary nodes 12,13,14 at 06:54 UTC. monitoring.
Kevin (eng-oncall): post-rollback: gateway 503s dropped to baseline in 3m. no further segfaults observed. keeping incident open for RCA.
Rana (sdet): repro after rollback: same synthetic burst ran 1000 requests, no worker exits.
Kevin (eng-oncall): next steps: 1) full canary audit to ensure no other pools have dynamic-resize enabled unintentionally; 2) add allocator guard to qbatcher dynamic path to pre-check large allocation and fallback to single-batch; 3) add better OOM metrics (per-runner allocation failures).
Sam (support): CS will notify customers with summary and follow-up. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident update: severity -> resolved for customer impact, postmortem-required
Kevin (eng-oncall): linking repro artifacts: s3://redwood-debug/1799998888/core-worker-183.log, heap profile, nvml-diagnostics.
Olivia (customer-success): putting note on customer tickets and scheduling follow-up tomorrow 09:00 PT.
Sam (support): closing loop for now, will keep thread open until postmortem posted.
